messages:
frank: deploy-bot just blocked the staging -> prod promotion for release 3.2.1 — attestation digest disagreement from eu-ecr mirror. holding rollout.

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: publish guard triggered for image redwood/service:3.2.1
provenance mismatch: attested_manifest=sha256:dde111... registry_manifest=sha256:ddf222...
metadata: build_id=202603201900, cosign=ok, attestation=present

carol: which region? I can check the ECR replication logs and S3 staging bucket.

frank: eu-west-1 (eu-ecr). deploy-bot says registry digest doesn't match the attestation payload. Could be a reordering rewrite or a late compacting step by the push proxy. We shouldn't promote until resolved.

greg: canary traffic looked fine for request/response, but we purposely skip heavy provenance lint outside gating. that probably explains why staging passed.

ben: any chance this is the known multi-part upload rewrite bug? I thought we had a mitigation.

carol: possible. looking at the push trace now — I'll tail the uploader logs.

deploy-bot: attach: /var/log/deploybot/publish/2026-03-20-19-00.log
```
2026-03-20T19:00:12Z INFO uploader: started multipart push
2026-03-20T19:00:31Z WARN registry-proxy: rewrite manifest order for dedupe
2026-03-20T19:00:45Z INFO attestor: created attestation (manifest=sha256:dde111...)
2026-03-20T19:00:47Z INFO registry: stored manifest sha256:ddf222...
2026-03-20T19:00:47Z ERROR provenance: attested manifest mismatch
```

hannah: if the registry rewrote the manifest after attestation the attestation will forever point to the old digest. options: 1) wait for replicas to converge (but attestation still points elsewhere), 2) re-publish the image with a canonical manifest (preferred), 3) push a new tag and do a canary under that tag.

frank: I'm leaning to option 2 or 3. we should avoid leaving the canonical tag ambiguous. I prefer reprovisioning under a new tag (3.2.1-rp1) and re-attest. less risky than changing the original tag.

ben: +1 to 3.2.1-rp1. also add a short release note entry that the original 3.2.1 was republished due to upstream manifest rewrite. include audit link.

carol: I can perform the republish. plan: pull layers from eu-ecr replica, canonicalize manifest (sort by digest), push as 3.2.1-rp1 in eu-ecr with explicit manifest digest, run cosign attest, and then update deploybot canary mapping.

deploy-bot: queued manual_republish by carol for build_id=202603201900.

carol: pulled blobs and verified local checksums; confirmed manifest ordering differed. recreating canonical manifest now.

carol: pushed 3.2.1-rp1 -> new digest sha256:ddg333... cosign attestation being uploaded.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: republish succeeded. attached attestation. registry_manifest=sha256:ddg333...

greg: starting full provenance lint + canary smoke on 3.2.1-rp1. will post failures if any.

hannah: I'll notify support and docs about the republish so changelog & release notes reflect the republished artifact.

frank: decision: do NOT promote original 3.2.1 tag. promote 3.2.1-rp1 to canary and run a controlled rollout if QA green. keep original tag pinned for 1 hour and create an incident note in the release audit.

ben: updating release checklist and changelog now. adding entry under "release-process notes".

carol: canary smoke is green (basic flows) and provenance lint passed. requesting manual gradual rollout with 5% initial traffic.

deploy-bot: manual rollout requested by carol: route 5% traffic to redwood/service:3.2.1-rp1.

greg: monitoring latency and error rate. will report back in 20m. so far looks normal.

frank: thanks for the quick turnaround. follow-up: we should add a gating check to run provenance lint earlier in the pipeline to catch this pre-promotion. I'll add a ticket. :thumbsup:
